question.worked_solution:
First, we find the first-order derivative ${g}_{y}(x,y):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{y}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)) \\  & =\frac{x}{x+y}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${g}_{yy}(x,y)$ by differentiating ${g}_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{yy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({g}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{x}{x+y}) \\  & =-\frac{x}{(x+y)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we find ${g}_{yyx}(x,y)$ by differentiating ${g}_{yy}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{yyx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({g}_{yy}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-\frac{x}{(x+y)^{2}}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{(x+y)^{2}}+\frac{2x}{(x+y)^{3}} \\  & =\frac{-(x+y)+2x}{(x+y)^{3}} \\  & =\frac{x-y}{(x+y)^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$
